Instructions for setting up pre-commit hooks and testing CDK additions in a development environment.

# Purpose
This documentation provides guidance on maintaining code quality and testing infrastructure changes within a monorepo for a software project. It outlines the setup and use of `pre-commit` hooks and the `Ruff` tool to enforce code standards automatically during development. The instructions include steps for installing `pre-commit` globally and setting up hooks that run linters on code changes. Additionally, the document describes a `test-in-dev` CDK stack used for testing infrastructure additions manually, as the current infrastructure does not support automated environment creation. The `test-in-dev` stack allows developers to test changes by modifying the `test_in_dev_stack.py` file and deploying with a specific environment variable. The document also includes notes on using AWS constructs and stacks, emphasizing the separation of logical units into constructs and the deployment of these units through stacks to enhance infrastructure reuse and deployment flexibility.
# Content Summary
The document provides instructions for setting up and maintaining code quality in the Driver AI Monorepo using pre-commit hooks and Ruff for linting and formatting. Developers are instructed to install pre-commit globally using Python or Homebrew. After installation, they must navigate to the root of the monorepo and run `pre-commit install` to set up the hooks defined in the `.pre-commit-config.yaml` file. These hooks automatically run Ruff and other linters during commits to ensure code quality and consistency. Developers can also manually run pre-commit hooks on all files using `pre-commit run --all-files`, though this may introduce many changes at once.

The document also addresses testing infrastructure changes using a `test-in-dev` CDK stack. This stack allows developers to test infrastructure additions manually, as the current infrastructure is not fully automated. Developers can modify the `test_in_dev_stack.py` file and deploy changes using the command `DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT=test-in-dev cdk deploy`. The mapping of the `DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT` variable to different stacks is managed in the `cdk_app.py` file, which can be customized for new test environments.

Additionally, the document includes guidance on using AWS constructs and stacks. Constructs should represent logical units of an application, while stacks are used for deployment. This approach enhances the reuse potential of infrastructure and provides flexibility in deployment scenarios.
